claim: Pentameric ligand-gated ion channels (pLGICs) mediate chemical signaling through a succession of allosteric transitions.
source: Pentameric ligand-gated ion channels (pLGICs) mediate chemical signaling through a succession of allosteric transitions that are yet not completely understood as intermediate states remain poorly characterized by structural approaches.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a general characterization of pLGICs function.

claim: Intermediate states in pLGIC allosteric transitions remain poorly characterized by structural approaches.
source: Pentameric ligand-gated ion channels (pLGICs) mediate chemical signaling through a succession of allosteric transitions that are yet not completely understood as intermediate states remain poorly characterized by structural approaches.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of current structural biology approaches in the abstract.

claim: GLIC is a prototypic bacterial proton-gated channel.
source: In a previous study on the prototypic bacterial proton-gated channel GLIC, we generated several fluorescent sensors of the protein conformation that report a fast transition to a pre-active state, which precedes the slower process of activation with pore opening.
evidence: This characterization of GLIC is stated in the abstract.

claim: Fluorescent sensors of GLIC report a fast transition to a pre-active state that precedes the slower process of activation with pore opening.
source: In a previous study on the prototypic bacterial proton-gated channel GLIC, we generated several fluorescent sensors of the protein conformation that report a fast transition to a pre-active state, which precedes the slower process of activation with pore opening.
evidence: This is a finding from a previous study by the authors, as stated in the abstract.

claim: Mutations at the subunit interface in the extracellular domain (ECD) principally alter pre-activation.
source: Our data, fitted to a three-state Monod-Wyman-Changeux model, show that mutations at the subunit interface in the extracellular domain (ECD) principally alter pre-activation, while mutations in the lower ECD and in the transmembrane domain principally alter activation.
evidence: This is a main finding from the current study based on MWC model fitting, as stated in the abstract.

claim: Mutations in the lower ECD and in the transmembrane domain principally alter activation.
source: Our data, fitted to a three-state Monod-Wyman-Changeux model, show that mutations at the subunit interface in the extracellular domain (ECD) principally alter pre-activation, while mutations in the lower ECD and in the transmembrane domain principally alter activation.
evidence: This is a main finding from the current study based on MWC model fitting, as stated in the abstract.

claim: Propofol alters both pre-activation and activation transitions in GLIC.
source: We also show that propofol alters both transitions.
evidence: This is stated as a finding in the abstract.

claim: Pre-activation involves major quaternary compaction of the ECD.
source: It further supports that pre-activation involves major quaternary compaction of the ECD, and suggests that activation involves principally a reorganization of a 'central gating region' involving a contraction of the ECD β-sandwich and the tilt of the channel lining M2 helix.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the abstract based on the study's data.

claim: Activation involves principally a reorganization of a 'central gating region' involving a contraction of the ECD β-sandwich and the tilt of the channel lining M2 helix.
source: It further supports that pre-activation involves major quaternary compaction of the ECD, and suggests that activation involves principally a reorganization of a 'central gating region' involving a contraction of the ECD β-sandwich and the tilt of the channel lining M2 helix.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the abstract based on the study's data.

claim: In mammals, the pLGIC family includes the excitatory nicotinic acetylcholine (ACh) and serotonin receptors (nAChRs and 5-HT3Rs).
source: In mammals, this family includes the excitatory nicotinic acetylcholine (ACh) and serotonin receptors (nAChRs and 5-HT3Rs) as well as the inhibitory γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) and glycine receptors (GABAARs and GlyRs) (Jaiteh et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to support the claim.

claim: In mammals, the pLGIC family includes the inhibitory γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) and glycine receptors (GABAARs and GlyRs).
source: In mammals, this family includes the excitatory nicotinic acetylcholine (ACh) and serotonin receptors (nAChRs and 5-HT3Rs) as well as the inhibitory γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) and glycine receptors (GABAARs and GlyRs) (Jaiteh et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to support the claim.

claim: pLGICs are present in bacteria, including the pH-gated channels GLIC and sTeLIC.
source: pLGICs are also present in bacteria, notably with the pH-gated channels GLIC (Bocquet et al., 2007) and sTeLIC (Hu et al., 2018), the GABA-gated channel ELIC (Zimmermann and Dutzler, 2011), and the calcium-modulated DeCLIC (Hu et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to support the claim.

claim: ELIC is a GABA-gated bacterial channel.
source: pLGICs are also present in bacteria, notably with the pH-gated channels GLIC (Bocquet et al., 2007) and sTeLIC (Hu et al., 2018), the GABA-gated channel ELIC (Zimmermann and Dutzler, 2011), and the calcium-modulated DeCLIC (Hu et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to support the claim.

claim: DeCLIC is a calcium-modulated bacterial channel.
source: pLGICs are also present in bacteria, notably with the pH-gated channels GLIC (Bocquet et al., 2007) and sTeLIC (Hu et al., 2018), the GABA-gated channel ELIC (Zimmermann and Dutzler, 2011), and the calcium-modulated DeCLIC (Hu et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to support the claim.

claim: A minimal four-state model could describe the main allosteric properties of the muscle-type nAChR.
source: Initially, a minimal four-state model could describe the main allosteric properties of the muscle-type nAChR (Heidmann and Changeux, 1980; Sakmann et al., 1980).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to support the claim.

claim: The ability of ACh binding to activate the nAChR involves a resting- to active-state transition.
source: In this model, the ability of ACh binding to activate the nAChR involves a resting- to active-state transition, and prolonged ACh occupancy promotes a biphasic desensitization process.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction describing the four-state model.

claim: Prolonged ACh occupancy promotes a biphasic desensitization process in nAChR.
source: In this model, the ability of ACh binding to activate the nAChR involves a resting- to active-state transition, and prolonged ACh occupancy promotes a biphasic desensitization process.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction describing the four-state model.

claim: Short-lived intermediate 'pre-active' states named 'flipped' were included in the kinetic schemes of GlyRs.
source: For activation, short-lived intermediate 'pre-active' states named 'flipped' (Lape et al., 2008) and 'primed' (Mukhtasimova et al., 2009) were included in the kinetic schemes of the GlyRs and nAChRs, while rate-equilibrium free-energy relationship analysis of numerous mutants of the nAChR suggested passage through four brief intermediate states (Gupta et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to support the claim.

claim: Short-lived intermediate 'pre-active' states named 'primed' were included in the kinetic schemes of nAChRs.
source: For activation, short-lived intermediate 'pre-active' states named 'flipped' (Lape et al., 2008) and 'primed' (Mukhtasimova et al., 2009) were included in the kinetic schemes of the GlyRs and nAChRs, while rate-equilibrium free-energy relationship analysis of numerous mutants of the nAChR suggested passage through four brief intermediate states (Gupta et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to support the claim.

claim: Rate-equilibrium free-energy relationship analysis of numerous mutants of the nAChR suggested passage through four brief intermediate states.
source: For activation, short-lived intermediate 'pre-active' states named 'flipped' (Lape et al., 2008) and 'primed' (Mukhtasimova et al., 2009) were included in the kinetic schemes of the GlyRs and nAChRs, while rate-equilibrium free-energy relationship analysis of numerous mutants of the nAChR suggested passage through four brief intermediate states (Gupta et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to support the claim.

claim: Analysis of single-channel shut intervals during desensitization is described by the sum of four or five exponential components.
source: Likewise, analysis of single-channel shut intervals during desensitization is described by the sum of four or five exponential components, suggesting again additional intermediate states (Elenes and Auerbach, 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to support the claim.

claim: pLGICs go through complex structural reorganizations during both activation and desensitization.
source: Kinetics data thus show that pLGICs go through complex structural reorganizations during both activation and desensitization.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from kinetic data in the introduction.

claim: The neurotransmitter site and the ion channel gate in pLGICs are separated by a distance of more than 50 Å.
source: These events are at the heart of the protein's function, allowing coupling between the neurotransmitter site and the ion channel gate which are separated by a distance of more than 50 Å.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a structural characteristic of pLGICs.

claim: At least one structure of each major member of prokaryotic pLGICs has been resolved by X-ray crystallography or cryo-electron microscopy (cryoEM).
source: At least one structure of each major member of prokaryotic (Hilf and Dutzler, 2008; Bocquet et al., 2009; Hu et al., 2018; Hu et al., 2020) and eukaryotic pLGICs (Althoff et al., 2014; Du et al., 2015; Polovinkin et al., 2018; Gharpure et al., 2019; Masiulis et al., 2019) have been resolved by X-ray crystallography or cryo-electron microscopy (cryoEM).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to support the claim.

claim: At least one structure of each major member of eukaryotic pLGICs has been resolved by X-ray crystallography or cryo-electron microscopy (cryoEM).
source: At least one structure of each major member of prokaryotic (Hilf and Dutzler, 2008; Bocquet et al., 2009; Hu et al., 2018; Hu et al., 2020) and eukaryotic pLGICs (Althoff et al., 2014; Du et al., 2015; Polovinkin et al., 2018; Gharpure et al., 2019; Masiulis et al., 2019) have been resolved by X-ray crystallography or cryo-electron microscopy (cryoEM).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to support the claim.

claim: pLGICs have a highly conserved 3D architecture within the family.
source: They highlight a highly conserved 3D architecture within the family.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a conclusion from structural studies.

claim: Each pLGIC subunit contains a large extracellular domain (ECD) folded in a β-sandwich.
source: Each subunit contains a large extracellular domain (ECD) folded in a β-sandwich and a transmembrane domain (TMD) containing four α-helices, with the second M2-helix lining the pore.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a structural characteristic of pLGICs.

claim: Each pLGIC subunit contains a transmembrane domain (TMD) containing four α-helices.
source: Each subunit contains a large extracellular domain (ECD) folded in a β-sandwich and a transmembrane domain (TMD) containing four α-helices, with the second M2-helix lining the pore.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a structural characteristic of pLGICs.

claim: The second M2-helix lines the pore in pLGICs.
source: Each subunit contains a large extracellular domain (ECD) folded in a β-sandwich and a transmembrane domain (TMD) containing four α-helices, with the second M2-helix lining the pore.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a structural characteristic of pLGICs.

claim: The physiological relevance of pLGIC structures or their assignment to particular intermediates or end-states in putative gating pathways remains ambiguous and poorly studied.
source: However, the physiological relevance of these structures or their assignment to particular intermediates or end-states in putative gating pathways remains ambiguous and poorly studied.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a limitation of current structural knowledge.

claim: Intermediate conformations, unfavored by crystal packing lattice or under-represented in receptor populations on cryoEM grids, may be missing in the current structural galleries.
source: Conversely, it is possible that intermediate conformations, unfavored by crystal packing lattice or under-represented in receptor populations on cryoEM grids, are missing in the current structural galleries.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a speculation about limitations of structural methods.

claim: The tryptophan/tyrosine induced quenching technique (TrIQ) was previously developed on GLIC.
source: To this aim, we previously developed the tryptophan/tyrosine induced quenching technique (TrIQ) on GLIC (Menny et al., 2017), a proton-gated channel (Parikh et al., 2011; Bocquet et al., 2007; Laha et al., 2013; Gonzalez-Gutierrez et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to the previous work.

claim: In the TrIQ technique, the protein is labeled with a small fluorophore bimane.
source: In this technique, the protein is labeled with a small fluorophore(bimane, and collisional quenching by a neighboring indole (tryptophan) or phenol (tyrosine) moiety is used to report on changes in distance between two residues within the protein over a short distance range of 5–15 Å (Mansoor et al., 2002; Mansoor et al., 2010; Jones Brunette and Farrens, 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction describing the TrIQ technique.

claim: Collisional quenching by a neighboring indole (tryptophan) or phenol (tyrosine) moiety is used to report on changes in distance between two residues within the protein over a short distance range of 5–15 Å.
source: In this technique, the protein is labeled with a small fluorophore(bimane, and collisional quenching by a neighboring indole (tryptophan) or phenol (tyrosine) moiety is used to report on changes in distance between two residues within the protein over a short distance range of 5–15 Å (Mansoor et al., 2002; Mansoor et al., 2010; Jones Brunette and Farrens, 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction describing the TrIQ technique with citations.

claim: Bimane-quencher pairs on GLIC combined with kinetic analysis allowed characterization of pre-activation motions occurring early in the conformational pathway of activation.
source: Bimane-quencher pairs on GLIC combined with kinetic analysis allowed us to characterize pre-activation motions occurring early in the conformational pathway of activation (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a finding from previous work.

claim: Pre-activation motions in GLIC occur at lower proton concentrations than pore opening.
source: We found that they occur at lower proton concentrations than pore opening, and are complete in less than a millisecond, much faster than the rise time of the active population that occurs in the 30–150 ms range in electrophysiology recordings (Laha et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a finding from previous work with a citation.

claim: Pre-activation motions in GLIC are complete in less than a millisecond.
source: We found that they occur at lower proton concentrations than pore opening, and are complete in less than a millisecond, much faster than the rise time of the active population that occurs in the 30–150 ms range in electrophysiology recordings (Laha et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a finding from previous work with a citation.

claim: The rise time of the active population in GLIC occurs in the 30–150 ms range in electrophysiology recordings.
source: We found that they occur at lower proton concentrations than pore opening, and are complete in less than a millisecond, much faster than the rise time of the active population that occurs in the 30–150 ms range in electrophysiology recordings (Laha et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to support the claim.

claim: Bim136-Q101W and Bim250-Y197 are sensors used in this study.
source: In the present study, we used the Bim136-Q101W as sensor of the ECD compaction, along with Bim250-Y197 as a sensor of the M2-M3 loop motion.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the quenching pairs used.

claim: Bim136-Q101W is a sensor of the ECD compaction.
source: In the present study, we used the Bim136-Q101W as sensor of the ECD compaction, along with Bim250-Y197 as a sensor of the M2-M3 loop motion.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the quenching pairs used.

claim: Bim250-Y197 is a sensor of the M2-M3 loop motion.
source: In the present study, we used the Bim136-Q101W as sensor of the ECD compaction, along with Bim250-Y197 as a sensor of the M2-M3 loop motion.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the quenching pairs used.

claim: pH-dependent fluorescence changes for Bim136-Q101W and Bim250-Y197 are essentially abolished when mutating the quenching partner to phenylalanine.
source: For both sensors, we confirmed that the pH-dependent fluorescence changes are essentially abolished when mutating the quenching partner to phenylalanine, which does not quench bimane fluorescence (Mansoor et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an experimental confirmation with a citation.

claim: Phenylalanine does not quench bimane fluorescence.
source: For both sensors, we confirmed that the pH-dependent fluorescence changes are essentially abolished when mutating the quenching partner to phenylalanine, which does not quench bimane fluorescence (Mansoor et al., 2002).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation to support the claim.

claim: pH-dependent quenching curves for Bim136-Q101W and Bim250-Y197 display higher sensitivity and lower apparent cooperativity than the pH-dependent activation curves recorded by electrophysiology.
source: We also confirmed that pH-dependent quenching curves for Bim136-Q101W and Bim250-Y197 display higher sensitivity (especially for Bim250-Y197) and lower apparent cooperativity than the pH-dependent activation curves recorded by electrophysiology (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: E26Q produces a decrease in pH50 for activation in GLIC.
source: We previously showed that E26Q produces a decrease in pH50 for activation (Nemecz et al., 2017), a phenotype that is conserved here on the Bim136-Q101W background (Figure 2B and C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation and supported by data in Figure 2B and C.

claim: The fluorescence quenching curve of Bim136-Q101W-E26Q shows a decrease in pH50.
source: The fluorescence quenching curve of Bim136-Q101W-E26Q also shows a decrease in pH50 (Figure 2D), and the ∆pH50 between Bim136-Q101W and Bim136-Q101W-E26Q are nearly identical in electrophysiology and fluorescence (−0.59 and −0.57, respectively; Table 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 2D and Table 1.

claim: The ∆pH50 between Bim136-Q101W and Bim136-Q101W-E26Q are nearly identical in electrophysiology and fluorescence (−0.59 and −0.57, respectively).
source: The fluorescence quenching curve of Bim136-Q101W-E26Q also shows a decrease in pH50 (Figure 2D), and the ∆pH50 between Bim136-Q101W and Bim136-Q101W-E26Q are nearly identical in electrophysiology and fluorescence (−0.59 and −0.57, respectively; Table 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Table 1.

claim: The Bim136-Q101W-E26Q fluorescence quenching curve shows significantly lower fluorescence (F0=0.53) at pH 7–8 compared to Bim136-Q101W alone (F0=0.71).
source: Interestingly, the Bim136-Q101W-E26Q fluorescence quenching curve has a remarkable feature as compared to most mutants investigated thereafter: in the pH 7–8 range, where the pH-dependent fluorescence quenching is not yet observed, the fluorescence (F/FSDS) is significantly lower (F0=0.53) as compared to the Bim136-Q101W alone (F0=0.71).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an observation from the data.

claim: E26Q not only alters the allosteric transition, but also modifies the conformation of the resting state itself which appears to be more compact when the E26Q mutation is present.
source: This suggests that substantial quenching is present at neutral pH and that E26Q not only alters the allosteric transition, but also modifies the conformation of the resting state itself which appears to be more compact when the E26Q mutation is present.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the fluorescence data.

claim: Y28F mutation in the Bim136-Q101W (C27S) background yields a drastic loss of function characterized by a slow activating receptor and a marked decrease in pH50.
source: Surprisingly, mutating Y28F in the Bim136-Q101W (C27S) background yields a drastic loss of function characterized by a slow activating receptor and a marked decrease in pH50 (Figure 2B and C; Table 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 2B and C and Table 1.

claim: Mutating back the C27 endogenous cysteine (Bim136-Q101W-Y28F (C27)) reverses the phenotype to that of Bim136-Q101W (C27S).
source: However, mutating back the C27 endogenous cysteine (Bim136-Q101W-Y28F (C27)) reverses the phenotype to that of Bim136-Q101W (C27S) (Figure 2C and Table 1), demonstrating that this loss of function is due to the combination of the C27S and Y28F mutations.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 2C and Table 1.

claim: The loss of function in Y28F is due to the combination of the C27S and Y28F mutations.
source: However, mutating back the C27 endogenous cysteine (Bim136-Q101W-Y28F (C27)) reverses the phenotype to that of Bim136-Q101W (C27S) (Figure 2C and Table 1), demonstrating that this loss of function is due to the combination of the C27S and Y28F mutations.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the experimental data.

claim: The quenching curve of Bim136-Q101W-Y28F (C27S) shows a large decrease in pH50 associated with an apparent higher cooperativity.
source: In fluorescence, the quenching curve of Bim136-Q101W-Y28F (C27S) also shows a large decrease in pH50, associated with an apparent higher cooperativity.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an observation from the fluorescence data.

claim: The quaternary compaction of the top of the ECD, monitored with the Bim136-Q101W sensor, is strongly coupled in an allosteric manner with the lower part of the ECD interface.
source: In conclusion, the quaternary compaction of the top of the ECD, monitored with the Bim136-Q101W sensor, is strongly coupled in an allosteric manner with the lower part of the ECD interface.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the Results section based on the mutational data.

claim: D32E, H235Q, and E222Q mutations show overall conservation of their previously published phenotype on the Bim136-Q101W-C27S background.
source: Performing these mutations on the Bim136-Q101W-C27S background shows overall conservation of their previously published phenotype, with a 0.7 unit (D32E and E222Q) and 1.3 unit (H235Q) decreases in the pH50 of activation as compared to Bim136-Q101W-C27S (Figure 3B and C; Table 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 3B and C and Table 1.

claim: D32E and E222Q show 0.7 unit decreases in the pH50 of activation as compared to Bim136-Q101W-C27S.
source: Performing these mutations on the Bim136-Q101W-C27S background shows overall conservation of their previously published phenotype, with a 0.7 unit (D32E and E222Q) and 1.3 unit (H235Q) decreases in the pH50 of activation as compared to Bim136-Q101W-C27S (Figure 3B and C; Table 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 3B and C and Table 1.

claim: H235Q shows 1.3 unit decrease in the pH50 of activation as compared to Bim136-Q101W-C27S.
source: Performing these mutations on the Bim136-Q101W-C27S background shows overall conservation of their previously published phenotype, with a 0.7 unit (D32E and E222Q) and 1.3 unit (H235Q) decreases in the pH50 of activation as compared to Bim136-Q101W-C27S (Figure 3B and C; Table 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 3B and C and Table 1.

claim: The fluorescence quenching curves for D32E, E222Q, and H235Q are shifted to lower pH50s, with ∆pH50s of 0.3–0.5 (D32E and E222Q) and 0.85 (H235Q).
source: The fluorescence quenching curves are also shifted to lower pH50s, with ∆pH50s of 0.3–0.5 (D32E and E222Q) and 0.85 (H235Q) (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 3D.

claim: The quenching data reveal an allosteric coupling between both ends of the protein, since the structural perturbations performed around the TMD are transmitted to the top of the ECD, impairing its compaction.
source: The quenching data thus reveal an allosteric coupling between both ends of the protein, since the structural perturbations performed around the TMD are transmitted to the top of the ECD, impairing its compaction.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the Results section based on the fluorescence data.

claim: D32E, E222Q, and H235Q mutations have a stronger effect on the pH50 of the electrophysiological response as compared to fluorescence quenching.
source: However, as opposed to the ECD mutations E26Q and Y28F/C27S, these mutations have a stronger effect on the pH50 of the electrophysiological response as compared to fluorescence quenching.
evidence: This is stated as an observation in the Results section comparing the effects of different mutations.

claim: Pre-activation and activation processes are not fully coupled for mutations further away from the sensor site.
source: It thus suggests that both processes are not fully coupled for mutations further away from the sensor site.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation in the Results section based on the differential effects of mutations.

claim: H235F, L157A, and L246A show robust surface expression and no substantial current in oocytes.
source: We selected three mutants: H235F, L157A, and L246A which show robust surface expression and no substantial current in oocytes (Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: L157A and L246A combined with Bim136-Q101W both show a pH-dependent quenching of fluorescence with a decreased amplitude (∆Fmax) associated with a significant decrease in pH50.
source: Mutants L157A and L246A reveal unique quenching phenotypes. Combined with Bim136-Q101W, they both show a pH-dependent quenching of fluorescence with a decreased amplitude (∆Fmax) associated with a significant decrease in pH50 as compared to the Bim136-Q101W background (Table 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Table 1.

claim: L157A and L246A only weakly alter the motions at Bim250, which occur with a complete amplitude and small changes in pH50.
source: In contrast, they only weakly alter the motions at Bim250, which occur with a complete amplitude and small changes in pH50.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an observation from the fluorescence data.

claim: H235F combined with Bim136-Q101W shows a nearly full quenching amplitude together with a decrease in pH50.
source: The mutation H235F leads to a phenotype opposite to that of L157A or L246A. Its Bim136-Q101W pH-dependent curve shows a nearly full quenching amplitude together with a decrease in pH50, while it impairs the motion of the M2-M3 loop, with only a partial pH-dependent de-quenching at Bim250-Y197.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an observation from the fluorescence data.

claim: H235F impairs the motion of the M2-M3 loop, with only a partial pH-dependent de-quenching at Bim250-Y197.
source: The mutation H235F leads to a phenotype opposite to that of L157A or L246A. Its Bim136-Q101W pH-dependent curve shows a nearly full quenching amplitude together with a decrease in pH50, while it impairs the motion of the M2-M3 loop, with only a partial pH-dependent de-quenching at Bim250-Y197.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an observation from the fluorescence data.

claim: H235F, L157A, and L246A mutants do not have a measurable access to the active state, but they still show allosteric motions as revealed by fluorescence.
source: Thus, while those mutants do not have a measurable access to the active state, they still show allosteric motions as revealed by fluorescence.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the Results section based on the fluorescence data.

claim: H235F, L157A, and L246A mutations alter the amplitude of the fluorescence curves, revealing profound changes of either the protein conformations and/or allosteric equilibria.
source: Unlike the moderate loss of function mutants investigated above, these mutations alter the amplitude of the fluorescence curves, revealing profound changes of either the protein conformations and/or allosteric equilibria.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation in the Results section based on the fluorescence data.

claim: Propofol binds to at least three main sites within the TMD of GLIC: one site in the pore itself near the middle of the TMD, and two sites in the upper part of the TMD at intra- or inter-subunit locations.
source: Propofol binds to at least three main sites within the TMD: one site in the pore itself near the middle of the TMD, and two sites in the upper part of the TMD at intra- or inter-subunit locations (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by Figure 5A showing the binding sites.

claim: Propofol is an inhibitor of GLIC.
source: Propofol is an inhibitor of GLIC, but it has been shown to be a potentiator of the H235Q mutant (Fourati et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation to support the claim.

claim: Propofol is a potentiator of the H235Q mutant of GLIC.
source: Propofol is an inhibitor of GLIC, but it has been shown to be a potentiator of the H235Q mutant (Fourati et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation to support the claim.

claim: Propofol decreases the pH50 of activation of Bim136-Q101W while increasing the pH50 of Bim136-Q101W-H235Q.
source: We verified that these effects are conserved in the Bim136-Q101W background, with propofol decreasing the pH50 of activation of Bim136-Q101W while increasing the pH50 of Bim136-Q101W-H235Q (Figure 5B and C; Table 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 5B and C and Table 1.

claim: Addition of 100 μM propofol on Bim136-Q101W decreases the fluorescence pH50 by half a unit.
source: Addition of 100 μM propofol on Bim136-Q101W decreases the fluorescence pH50 by half a unit, while it increases that of Bim136-Q101W-H235Q by more than half a unit (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 5D.

claim: Addition of 100 μM propofol on Bim136-Q101W-H235Q increases the fluorescence pH50 by more than half a unit.
source: Addition of 100 μM propofol on Bim136-Q101W decreases the fluorescence pH50 by half a unit, while it increases that of Bim136-Q101W-H235Q by more than half a unit (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 5D.

claim: Propofol acts on the global allosteric transitions by displacing the equilibria of both pre-activation and activation.
source: Our data thus shows that propofol does act on the global allosteric transitions by displacing the equilibria of both pre-activation and activation.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the Results section based on the fluorescence and electrophysiology data.

claim: Propofol binding into the pore may sterically block ion translocation to produce inhibition.
source: It is noteworthy that propofol is also likely to generate local effects upon binding to modulate the function, which are not investigated here. For instance, its binding into the pore may sterically block ion translocation to produce inhibition (Fourati et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as a speculation in the Results section with a citation.

claim: A three-state MWC model was used to fit the whole data set, where the protein is in equilibrium between a resting R state, a pre-active pA state, and an active A state.
source: To characterize the effect of mutations in a more quantitative manner, we fitted the whole data set with a Monod-Wyman-Changeux (MWC) model. Since the fluorescence and electrophysiological pH-dependent curves presented here underlie two major allosteric steps, pre-activation (a fast process causing the changes in fluorescence as previously identified in stopped flow experiments; Menny et al., 2017) and activation (a slower process responsible for channel opening), we used a three-state model where the protein is in equilibrium between a resting R state, a pre-active pA state, and an active A state.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the modeling approach.

claim: Changes in fluorescence, although measured in equilibrium conditions, actually occur with fast kinetics and are likely not related to desensitization.
source: Changes in fluorescence, although measured here in equilibrium conditions, actually occur with fast kinetics and are likely not related to desensitization.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the fluorescence data.

claim: Peak currents recorded in oocytes were used for the measure of activation, assuming that desensitization would be negligible in these conditions.
source: For the measure of activation, we used peak currents recorded in oocytes, assuming that desensitization would be negligible in these conditions.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the experimental approach.

claim: The putative slow-desensitized state of GLIC was not included in the MWC model.
source: The putative slow-desensitized state of GLIC was thus not included in this model.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the modeling approach.

claim: A three-state model comprising a single proton site could not account for the separation between the fluorescence and electrophysiological curves.
source: Keeping the pre-activation parameters defined above, we found that a three-state model comprising a single proton site could not account for the separation between the fluorescence and electrophysiological curves.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a finding from the modeling.

claim: A second proton site was added to the model that specifically drives the activation step.
source: To fit the activation curves, we thus added a second proton site (named primed, present in five copies), that specifically drives the activation step (KR'=KpA', KpA'>KA'), while the first proton site specifically drives the pre-activation step (KR>KpA, KpA=KA).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the modeling approach.

claim: Several proton sites are contributing to GLIC activation.
source: This model is reasonable since it is established that several proton sites are contributing to GLIC activation (Nemecz et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a citation to support the modeling approach.

claim: Y28F is fitted by the assumption that the R-pA equilibrium is strongly displaced toward the R state, with no changes in the pA to A equilibrium.
source: Y28F is readily fitted by the simple assumption that the R-pA equilibrium is strongly displaced toward the R state, that is, the R state is thermodynamically stabilized over both the pA and A states, with no changes in the pA to A equilibrium.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a finding from the MWC model fitting.

claim: For Y28F mutant, the fraction of receptors in the pA state, in equilibrium conditions, remains below 0.1% at every pH.
source: In this condition, the fluorescent changes are entirely caused by the apparition of the active state, and the fraction of receptors in the pA state, in these equilibrium conditions, remains below 0.1% at every pH.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a finding from the MWC model fitting.

claim: E26Q has a stronger effect on pre-activation than on activation (multiplication factors of isomerization constants of 15 for pre-activation and 10 for activation).
source: Mutant E26Q has a milder phenotype, but the fitting also suggests it has a stronger effect on pre-activation than on activation (multiplication factors of isomerization constants of 15 for pre-activation and 10 for activation, Figure 6B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 6B.

claim: D32E, H235Q, and E222Q are found to preferentially alter the activation transition, destabilizing the A state over the pA state, with small effects on pre-activation.
source: In contrast, mutants in the lower ECD (D32E), or in the TMD (H235Q and E222Q), are found to preferentially alter the activation transition, destabilizing the A state over the pA state, with small effects on pre-activation (multiplication factor of isomerization constants for pre-activation: 2, 1.5, and 7 and for activation: 80, 40, and 700, respectively).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a finding from the MWC model fitting.

claim: For both Bim136-Q101W and H235Q mutant, propofol has a dual effect, altering principally the activation transition but also the pre-activation transition.
source: On the Bim136-Q101W sensor and H235Q mutant, propofol acts respectively as a negative and positive allosteric modulator (Fourati et al., 2018). For both constructs, propofol is found to have a dual effect, altering principally the activation transition but also the pre-activation transition.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a finding from the MWC model fitting with a citation.

claim: H235F fluorescence quenching could be fitted reasonably well with a two-state R-pA model.
source: Finally, for total loss of function mutants, while H235F fluorescence quenching could be fitted reasonably well with a two-state R-pA model (Figure 7, Figure 6—figure supplement 2—source data 1) the best fits of L157A and L246A were of lower quality.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a finding from the MWC model fitting.

claim: The best fits of L157A and L246A were of lower quality compared to H235F.
source: Finally, for total loss of function mutants, while H235F fluorescence quenching could be fitted reasonably well with a two-state R-pA model (Figure 7, Figure 6—figure supplement 2—source data 1) the best fits of L157A and L246A were of lower quality.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a finding from the MWC model fitting.

claim: L157A and L246A mutants display complex phenotypes, plausibly driving the conformations into states that are not implemented in the MWC model.
source: The tentative fits are thus not satisfactory, suggesting that these mutants display complex phenotypes, plausibly driving the conformations into states that are not implemented in our model.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the modeling results.

claim: GLIC-pH 7 is in a non-conductive conformation with a closed hydrophobic gate in the upper part of the pore, consistent with a resting-like state.
source: GLIC-pH 7 is in a non-conductive conformation with a closed hydrophobic gate in the upper part of the pore, consistent with a resting-like state.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a characterization of the GLIC-pH 7 structure.

claim: The GLIC-pH 4 structure shows an open gate compatible with a conductive conformation consistent with an active-like structure.
source: The GLIC-pH 4 structure shows in contrast an open gate compatible with a conductive conformation (Cheng and Coalson, 2010; Fritsch et al., 2011; Sauguet et al., 2013; Gonzalez-Gutierrez et al., 2017) consistent with an active-like structure.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with citations to support the characterization.

claim: Two independent trajectories were computed using iMODfit: Trajectory A starts from the closed GLIC-pH 7 structure to reach the open GLIC-pH 4 structure, and trajectory B starts from the GLIC-pH 4 structure to reach the GLIC-pH 7 structure.
source: Two independent trajectories were computed. Trajectory A (12 frames) starts from the closed GLIC-pH 7 structure to reach the open GLIC-pH 4 structure, and trajectory B (11 frames) starts from the GLIC-pH 4 structure to reach the GLIC-pH 7 structure.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section describing the computational approach.

claim: Both trajectories, when visualized from the resting to active state, show three major reorganizations components: a quaternary twist of the pentamer, a 'central gating reorganization' comprising opening/closure of the pore, and a quaternary compaction of the ECD.
source: Both trajectories, when visualized from the resting to active state, show three major reorganizations components: a quaternary twist of the pentamer, a 'central gating reorganization' comprising opening/closure of the pore, and a quaternary compaction of the ECD.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a finding from the iMODfit calculations.

claim: In trajectory A, the twist motion occurs in the first half of the trajectory.
source: In trajectory A, the twist motion occurs in the first half of the trajectory (Figure 8B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 8B.

claim: In trajectory A, the pore reorganization happens in the second half of the trajectory and leads to the opening of its upper part which contains the activation gate.
source: The pore reorganization happens in the second half of the trajectory and leads to the opening of its upper part which contains the activation gate, as measured at Ile233 Cα (also named I9'; Figure 9A and B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 9A and B.

claim: The pore reorganization in trajectory A is associated with a central gating reorganization involving: a tilt of M2 toward M3, an outward motion of the M2-M3 loop, and a contraction of the β-sandwich at the bottom of the ECD.
source: This motion is associated with a central gating reorganization of the GLIC structure involving: 1/ a tilt of M2 toward M3 (as measured by a decrease in distance between His235 nitrogen and the carbonyl backbone of Ile259; Figure 9A and C), 2/ an outward motion of the M2-M3 loop (measured as an increase in distance between Pro250 Cα and the phenolic oxygen of Tyr197; Figure 9A and D), and 3/ a contraction of the β-sandwich at the bottom of the ECD (measured as a decrease in distance between Cα of residues Asp32 and Gly159; Figure 10).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figures 9 and 10.

claim: The progressive quaternary compaction of the ECD occurs throughout trajectory A.
source: In addition to these two consecutive global motions, the progressive quaternary compaction of the ECD, another crucial landmark of GLIC reorganization, occurs throughout the trajectory.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a finding from the iMODfit calculations.

claim: Trajectory B shows substantially the same components as trajectory A but with an inverted sequence of events.
source: Trajectory B shows substantially the same components but with an inverted sequence of events.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a finding from the iMODfit calculations.

claim: In trajectory B, the central gating reorganization starts first and is associated with an increase in pore radius at Ile233, followed by the twist motion in the second half of the trajectory.
source: The central gating reorganization starts first and is associated with an increase in pore radius at Ile233, followed by the twist motion in the second half of the trajectory, the latter being associated with further fluctuations of the pore radius.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a finding from the iMODfit calculations.

claim: For Bim136-Q101W, Bim136 and the Trp101 indole ring are separated in the resting-like state and are in close contact in the active-like state.
source: For Bim136-Q101W, the procedure shows that Bim136 and the Trp101 indole ring are separated in the resting-like state (first frame of both trajectories), and are in close contact in the active-like state (last frames of both trajectories) (Figure 10A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 10A.

claim: The trajectory A for Bim136-Q101W shows a progressive decrease in distance that parallels the ECD quaternary compaction movement.
source: The trajectory A shows a progressive decrease in distance that parallels the ECD quaternary compaction movement (Cβ Asp136/Gln101).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a finding from the bimane docking calculations.

claim: The trajectory B for Bim136-Q101W shows important fluctuations followed by a sharper distance decrease only in the last frames.
source: The trajectory B shows a different pattern, characterized by important fluctuations followed by a sharper distance decrease only in the last frames (Figure 10C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 10C.

claim: For Bim250-Y197, Bim250 is in close contact with the Tyr197 phenol ring in the resting-like state, while both moieties are separated in the active-like state.
source: For the ECD-TMD interface quenching pair Bim250-Y197, the procedure shows that Bim250 is in close contact with the Tyr197 phenol ring in the resting-like state, while both moieties are separated in the active-like state, the bimane moiety moving on the other side of loop 2 (Figure 9A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 9A.

claim: Both trajectories A and B for Bim250-Y197 show an abrupt change in Bim250-Y197 distances, corresponding respectively to a late versus early separation, and these changes occur during the outward motion of the M2-M3 loop.
source: Interestingly, both trajectories A and B show an abrupt change in Bim250-Y197 distances, corresponding respectively to a late versus early separation, and these changes occur during the outward motion of the M2-M3 loop (P250Cα/Y197O distance; Figure 9D).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 9D.

claim: Visualizing the quenching pairs using a simple docking procedure shows good agreement with fluorescence.
source: In conclusion, visualizing the quenching pairs using a simple docking procedure shows good agreement with fluorescence.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the Results section based on the docking calculations.

claim: At position P250, data show a clear switch of bimane from one side of loop 2 to the other during the quenching/dequenching process.
source: At position P250, data also show a clear switch of bimane from one side of loop 2 to the other during the quenching/dequenching process.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the Results section based on the docking calculations.

claim: Bim136-Q101W and Bim250-Y197 sensors are bona fide reporters of the ECD compaction and the outward M2-M3 motion, respectively.
source: In this study, we revisited several fluorescent sensors by performing detailed pH-dependent quenching curves and parallel iMODfit/docking calculations. Our data clearly support that Bim136-Q101W and Bim250-Y197 sensors are bona fide reporters of the ECD compaction and the outward M2-M3 motion, respectively.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the Discussion section based on the study's data.

claim: A series of five loss-of-function mutations shift the pH-dependent electrophysiological curves to higher concentrations and also shift the pH-dependent fluorescence quenching curve of ECD-compaction at the extracellular top of the protein.
source: Using these appropriate sensors, we found that a series of five loss-of-function mutations, which shift the pH-dependent electrophysiological curves to higher concentrations, also shift the pH-dependent fluorescence quenching curve of ECD-compaction at the extracellular top of the protein.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a summary of the findings.

claim: The ECD-compaction is sensitive to mutations scattered along the protein structure down to the opposite cytoplasmic end, indicating substantial allosteric coupling.
source: The ECD-compaction is thus sensitive to mutations scattered along the protein structure down to the opposite cytoplasmic end, indicating substantial allosteric coupling.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a conclusion from the mutational data.

claim: E26Q and Y28F/C27S mutations mainly impact the pre-activation transition.
source: Mutations in the ECD E26Q and Y28F/C27S both present such a phenotype with similar ∆pH50 in electrophysiology and fluorescence, suggesting that those mutations would mainly impact the pre-activation transition.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an interpretation of the data.

claim: D32E, E222Q, and H235Q mutations alter not only the pre-activation, but also the downstream pore-opening transitions leading to an additive effect on the pH50.
source: In contrast, D32E, E222Q, and H235Q lead to a stronger pH50 shift in electrophysiology than in fluorescence suggesting that these mutations would alter not only the pre-activation, but also the downstream pore-opening transitions leading to an additive effect on the pH50.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an interpretation of the data.

claim: Two proton binding sites had to be implemented in the MWC model to account for the separation of the fluorescence and electrophysiological curves of most constructs.
source: We had to implement two proton binding sites to account for the separation of the fluorescence and electrophysiological curves of most constructs.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a description of the modeling approach.

claim: Several proton activation sites, located at multiple loci, contribute to GLIC activation.
source: This idea is supported by a mutational analysis that showed that several proton activation sites, located at multiple loci, contribute to activation (Nemecz et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a citation to support the modeling approach.

claim: Chimeric receptors made up of the GLICECD fused to the TMDs of various pLGICs all preserve a proton-gated ion channel function.
source: In addition, chimeric receptors made up of the GLICECD fused to the TMDs of various pLGICs (Duret et al., 2011; Ghosh et al., 2017; Laverty et al., 2017) or of the ELICECD fused to the GLICTMD (Schmandt et al., 2015) all preserve a proton-gated ion channel function, with the GLICECD-GABAρTMD chimera showing a markedly biphasic pH-dependent activation curve (Ghosh et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations to support the claim.

claim: The GLICECD-GABAρTMD chimera shows a markedly biphasic pH-dependent activation curve.
source: In addition, chimeric receptors made up of the GLICECD fused to the TMDs of various pLGICs (Duret et al., 2011; Ghosh et al., 2017; Laverty et al., 2017) or of the ELICECD fused to the GLICTMD (Schmandt et al., 2015) all preserve a proton-gated ion channel function, with the GLICECD-GABAρTMD chimera showing a markedly biphasic pH-dependent activation curve (Ghosh et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a citation to support the claim.

claim: The proton activation sites in GLIC are scattered throughout the structure, in both the ECD and the TMD.
source: This suggests that the proton activation sites, whose loci are not known, are scattered throughout the GLIC structure, in both the ECD and the TMD.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an inference from the chimera data.

claim: Y28F and E26Q principally alter the pre-activation transition.
source: As anticipated from measured ∆pH50, the fits illustrate that Y28F and E26Q principally alter the pre-activation transition and that Bim250, D32E, H235Q, and E222Q principally alter the activation transition, while propofol alters similarly both processes (Figure 11).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by data in Figure 11.

claim: Bim250, D32E, H235Q, and E222Q principally alter the activation transition.
source: As anticipated from measured ∆pH50, the fits illustrate that Y28F and E26Q principally alter the pre-activation transition and that Bim250, D32E, H235Q, and E222Q principally alter the activation transition, while propofol alters similarly both processes (Figure 11).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by data in Figure 11.

claim: Propofol alters similarly both pre-activation and activation processes.
source: As anticipated from measured ∆pH50, the fits illustrate that Y28F and E26Q principally alter the pre-activation transition and that Bim250, D32E, H235Q, and E222Q principally alter the activation transition, while propofol alters similarly both processes (Figure 11).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by data in Figure 11.

claim: H235F isomerizes to a pre-active-like state but cannot isomerize further to the active state.
source: H235F is acceptably fitted according to an R-pA model, suggesting that this mutant isomerizes to a pre-active-like state but cannot isomerize further to the active state.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an interpretation of the modeling results.

claim: L257A and L246A show a more complex phenotype, but fluorescence data show at least partial pre-active-like motions.
source: L257A and L246A show a more complex phenotype, but fluorescence data show at least partial pre-active-like motions.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an interpretation of the fluorescence data.

claim: Pre-activation involves a major quaternary compaction of the whole ECD.
source: The ECD quenching pairs at Bim136, Bim133, and Bim33 already showed that pre-activation involves a major quaternary compaction of the whole ECD.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a conclusion from previous and current data.

claim: Pre-activation involves a key outward movement of the M2-M3 loop.
source: In addition, the quenching pair at Bim250 showed that the pre-activation involved a key outward movement of the M2-M3 loop.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a conclusion from the data.

claim: Pre-activation includes motions of the TMD, since mutation H235Q, as well as propofol binding, are shown to significantly alter pre-activation.
source: Our data indicate that pre-activation also includes motions of the TMD, since mutation H235Q, as well as propofol binding, are shown to significantly alter pre-activation.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a conclusion from the data.

claim: Activation involves a key role of the lower inner part of the ECD β-sandwich (D32E), the M2-M3 loop (Bim250), and the TMD (H235F/Q and E222Q).
source: For the activation, our mutational analysis points to a key role of the lower inner part of the ECD β-sandwich (D32E), the M2-M3 loop (Bim250), and the TMD (H235F/Q and E222Q).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a conclusion from the mutational data.

claim: D32E is involved in strong interactions between sheets in the lower part of the β-sandwich through a salt bridge with R192.
source: Interestingly, D32E is involved in strong interactions between sheets in the lower part of the β-sandwich through a salt bridge with R192 (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section and supported by Figure 3A.

claim: Mutation D32E, elongating the side chain by one carbon atom, is predicted to disfavor the β-sandwich compaction.
source: Mutation, D32E, elongating the side chain by one carbon atom is thus predicted to disfavor the β-sandwich compaction.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a prediction based on structural considerations.

claim: H235 from M2 interacts with the main-chain carbonyl of I259 from M3 through an H-bond favoring the interaction between both helices.
source: In addition, at the middle of the TMD, H235 from M2 interacts with the main-chain carbonyl of I259 from M3 through an H-bond favoring the interaction between both helices (Prevost et al., 2012; Rienzo et al., 2014; Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations and supported by Figure 3A.

claim: Mutation of H235 into Q and F is predicted to weaken or abolish the interaction between M2 and M3 and disfavor the tilt of M2 toward M3.
source: Its mutation into Q and F is predicted to weaken or abolish this interaction and disfavor the tilt of M2 toward M3.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a prediction based on structural considerations.

claim: The X-ray structure of the H235F and H235Q mutants shows a 'locally closed conformation' where M2 and M3 are separated.
source: This assumption is consistent with the X-ray structure of the H235F and H235Q mutants which shows a 'locally closed conformation' where M2 and M3 are separated (Prevost et al., 2012; Fourati et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations to support the claim.

claim: The compaction of the β-sandwich and the tilt of M2 are principally involved in the activation process.
source: Our data thus provide evidence that the compaction of the β-sandwich and the tilt of M2 are principally involved in the activation process.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a conclusion from the data.

claim: Most mutations show mixed effects on the isomerization constants of activation and pre-activation, suggesting that both processes involve overlapping regions.
source: The mutational analysis also shows for most mutations mixed effects on the isomerization constants of activation and pre-activation, suggesting that both processes involve overlapping regions.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an interpretation of the modeling results.

claim: The M2-M3 loop could move in two successive steps, a first one during pre-activation conditioning dequenching and a second one during activation.
source: It is thus plausible that the M2-M3 loop could move in two successive steps, a first one during pre-activation conditioning dequenching and a second one during activation.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a speculation based on the data.

claim: The transition pathway of GLIC has been previously studied by atomic-level molecular dynamics simulations in an explicit membrane environment.
source: The transition pathway of GLIC has been previously studied by atomic-level molecular dynamics simulations in an explicit membrane environment.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as background information.

claim: A 1 μs simulation starting from the GLIC-pH 4 structure set to neutral pH yielded concomitant closing of the pore and twist of the whole structure.
source: The first one started from the GLIC-pH 4 structure and instantly set it to neutral pH, followed by a 1 μs simulation (Nury et al., 2010), yielding concomitant closing of the pore and twist of the whole structure.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a citation to support the claim.

claim: A trajectory computed using the string method between GLIC-pH 7 and GLIC-pH 4 shows a sequence of events starting from the closed to the open conformation.
source: The second one is based on the string method, using the 'swarms of trajectories' approach, computing a trajectory between GLIC-pH 7 and GLIC-pH 4 (Lev et al., 2017). The trajectory shows a sequence of events starting from the closed to the open conformation.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a citation to support the claim.

claim: In the string method trajectory, a first major reorganization involves the opening of the pore, its hydration, and the compaction of the lower part of the ECD β-sandwich, followed by a major reorganization of the ECD, notably its twist and its quaternary compaction.
source: A first major reorganization involves the opening of the pore, its hydration, and the compaction of the lower part of the ECD β-sandwich. This is followed by a major reorganization of the ECD, notably its twist and its quaternary compaction.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section describing the string method trajectory with a citation.

claim: The sequence of events in the string method trajectory appears hardly compatible with the quenching data from this study.
source: This sequence of events appears hardly compatible with our quenching data, although a comprehensive integration of both sets of data would require extensive in silico investigations of the bimane-labeled mutants to analyze the reorganizations of the quenching pairs.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an assessment of the compatibility between different approaches.

claim: Both iMODfit trajectories show complex quaternary asymmetric reorganizations of ECD compaction.
source: Remarkably, both trajectories show complex quaternary asymmetric reorganizations of ECD compaction.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a finding from the iMODfit calculations.

claim: ECD compaction is critically involved in pre-activation, a feature consistent with recent work by electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopy showing a proton-induced inward tilting motion of the ECDs.
source: As stated above, ECD compaction is critically involved in pre-activation, a feature consistent with recent work by electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopy (Tiwari et al., 2020) showing a proton-induced inward tilting motion of the ECDs, and recent cryoEM work showing marked structural flexibility of the ECD in the closed-channel state at pH 7 (Rovsnik et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations to support the claim.

claim: Recent cryoEM work shows marked structural flexibility of the ECD in the closed-channel state at pH 7.
source: As stated above, ECD compaction is critically involved in pre-activation, a feature consistent with recent work by electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopy (Tiwari et al., 2020) showing a proton-induced inward tilting motion of the ECDs, and recent cryoEM work showing marked structural flexibility of the ECD in the closed-channel state at pH 7 (Rovsnik et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a citation to support the claim.

claim: The low cooperativity of fluorescence curves of pre-activation might arise from the contribution of multiple asymmetric intermediate states to the transition.
source: Interestingly, fluorescence curves of pre-activation, especially the one of Bim136-Q101W, are endowed with markedly low cooperativities. We thus speculate that this low cooperativity might arise from the contribution of multiple asymmetric intermediate states to the transition, in a manner reminiscent of the asymmetric motions recently described for the desensitization of the GABAA receptor (Gielen et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a speculation with a citation.

claim: Both iMODfit trajectories show a 'central gating motion' involving several key concerted reorganizations: a compaction of the lower part of the β-sandwich, an outward movement of the M2-M3 loop, as well as a tilt of the M2 helix toward M3, that involves a marked increase in the opening of the pore.
source: In addition, both trajectories show a 'central gating motion' involving several key concerted reorganizations: a compaction of the lower part of the β-sandwich, an outward movement of the M2-M3 loop, as well as a tilt of the M2 helix toward M3, that involves a marked increase in the opening of the pore.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a finding from the iMODfit calculations.

claim: Similar structural couplings to the 'central gating motion' are also observed in string simulations.
source: Similar structural couplings are also observed in string simulations (Lev et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a citation to support the claim.

claim: The central gating motion constitutes the heart of the activation transition.
source: This observation nicely parallels our finding that these motions are principally involved in activation. We can thus speculate that the central gating motion constitutes the heart of the activation transition.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a speculation based on the data.

claim: Trajectory A is a better fit to the fluorescence data than trajectory B.
source: Concerning the order in which reorganizations are observed, trajectory A is a better fit to the fluorescence data.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as an assessment of the trajectories.

claim: Trajectory A suggests a scenario involving, during pre-activation, progressive ECD compaction and beginning of the M2-M3 loop motion, generating the fluorescence variations, then the M2-M3 loop completes its movement in concert with β-sandwich compaction and pore opening.
source: It suggests a scenario involving, during pre-activation, progressive ECD compaction and beginning of the M2-M3 loop motion, generating the fluorescence variations. Then the M2-M3 loop completes its movement in concert with β-sandwich compaction and pore opening.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a speculation based on trajectory A.

claim: The conservation of the general gating mechanism between bacterial and eukaryotic pLGICs is well documented by the available structures with the common allosteric regulatory sites for ligands and mutations.
source: The conservation of the general gating mechanism between bacterial and eukaryotic pLGICs is well documented by the available structures with the common allosteric regulatory sites for ligands and mutations (Sauguet et al., 2015; Bertozzi et al., 2016; Rienzo et al., 2016), together with the allosteric compatibility between eukaryotic and prokaryotic ECD/TMD domains to form functional chimeras (Duret et al., 2011; Moraga-Cid et al., 2015; Laverty et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations to support the claim.

claim: The pre-activation transition of GLIC might have counterparts in human neurotransmitter-gated receptors.
source: It is therefore tempting to speculate that the pre-activation transition of GLIC that we characterize here might have counterparts in human neurotransmitter-gated receptors.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a speculation.

claim: Some recent structures of eukaryotic receptors including the 5-HT3R, the GABAAR and the GlyR show pre-active-like conformations characterized by marked agonist-elicited reorganization of the ECD but a closed channel at the TMD.
source: In this line, some recent structures of eukaryotic receptors including the 5-HT3R (Polovinkin et al., 2018), the GABAAR (Masiulis et al., 2019) and the GlyR (Yu et al., 2021) show pre-active-like conformations characterized by marked agonist-elicited reorganization of the ECD but a closed channel at the TMD.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations to support the claim.

claim: The flipped or primed states, where the conformational change of the orthosteric site is predicted to be complete, but where the channel is closed, would fit the functional requirement of a pre-active state.
source: Additionally, the flipped or primed states, where the conformational change of the orthosteric site is predicted to be complete, but where the channel is closed, would fit the functional requirement of a pre-active state (Lape et al., 2008; Plested, 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with citations to support the claim.

claim: Most of the hot spots mutated in GLIC were found associated with pathologies on human receptors.
source: Most of the hot spots mutated here on GLIC were found associated with pathologies on human receptors.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a comparison between GLIC and human receptors.

claim: The lower part of the ECD-ECD interface is the site of a de novo S76R mutation in GABAA α1 (homologous to Glu26) causing epilepsy.
source: In particular, the lower part of the ECD-ECD interface is the site of a de novo S76R mutation in GABAA α1 (homologous to Glu26) causing epilepsy (Johannesen, 2016) and the mutation L42P in the nAChR δ (homologous to Cys27) causing myasthenia (Shen et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a citation to support the claim.

claim: The mutation L42P in the nAChR δ (homologous to Cys27) causes myasthenia.
source: In particular, the lower part of the ECD-ECD interface is the site of a de novo S76R mutation in GABAA α1 (homologous to Glu26) causing epilepsy (Johannesen, 2016) and the mutation L42P in the nAChR δ (homologous to Cys27) causing myasthenia (Shen et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a citation to support the claim.

claim: The mutation L42P in nAChR δ decreases activation kinetics.
source: This latter mutation (as well as mutation of N41, homologous to E26) decreases activation kinetics and this residue was shown to be energetically coupled to Y127 on the other side of the interface.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as a characterization of the mutation.

claim: The mutation P250T in GlyR α1 causes hyperekplexia.
source: Another noteworthy example is the mutation P250T in GlyR α1 that causes hyperekplexia (Saul et al., 1999) and which is homologous to E222 in GLIC.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a citation to support the claim.

claim: On the glycine receptor α1, the mutation A52S in the loop 2 at the ECD-ECD interface affects principally a flip pre-activation-like step.
source: Interestingly, on the glycine receptor α1, other mutations have been studied by single-channel recordings and are described to affect principally a flip pre-activation-like step for A52S in the loop 2 at the ECD-ECD interface (Plested et al., 2007) or gating for K276E on the M2-M3 loop (Lape et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a citation to support the claim.
